options.reason: No liquid single-stock option market in Japan for this name. JPX option volume is concentrated in the index, so there is no event-implied move and no skew. Until 2026-09-18 that left priced_lean_pct as -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, which is ALSO the free control, so the baseline's lean and its own benchmark were the same number. They are no longer: `positioning` and `expected_move` below carry substitutes built from what Tokyo does publish, and this baseline supplies its own `priced_lean_pct` and `anchor_quality`.

history.caveat: Announcement DATES are estimated by applying this quarter's notified lag backwards to prior period ends; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate. This is a cadence prior, not a record that a print happened on that date. Use it as a scale for how much this name moves, never as evidence about a particular past date.

event_plausibility.basis: issuer-notified date carried by JPX on the 決算発表予定日 sheet

positioning.basis: absent from the JPX register, so no disclosed position at or above the 0.5% threshold. A real zero, not missing data -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0.
positioning.margin_ratio_basis: 信用倍率, margin long balance / margin short balance, scraped from a broker portal rather than published by the exchange. Null is a normal outcome.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of twelve ESTIMATED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it, and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read researcher_japan/scripts/jp_priced_in.py, lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR, none is measured on Japanese data, and jp_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters today is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus an estimated-cadence reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the three positioning components resolved, capped at 0.60 because none of them is 25-delta skew.

evidence.text: Fujiya's held FY2026 OP plan of 3,200m implies H2 OP of 2,903m (+77% y/y) after H1 OP of 297m (12.5% progress against 47-53% at the same point in 2024-2025), while Q3 is seasonally a loss quarter (Q3 OP -314m in 2024, -133m in 2025) and the record Q4 OP is 1,771m (2025); a downward revision at this Q3 print has a direct company precedent (2023-10-24, OP cut 29% at the Q3 release) and a counter-precedent (2024-10-28, plan held at 21.5% Q3 progress, cut separately on 2025-01-27).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Next-session moves from Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/2211.T?range=5y&interval=1d): 2023-10-24 Q3 print with a 29% OP cut -1.06%; 2024-01-26 separate second cut -2.47%; 2024-10-28 Q3 print, plan held at 21.5% progress -0.87%; 2025-01-27 separate 36% OP cut -1.03%; 2026-07-28 H1 miss with plan held +1.25% (悪材料出尽くし). evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the H1 progress rate has been computable since 2026-07-28, and the stock trades at PER 31x on plan EPS 81.5, a multiple that only makes sense if holders already look past the plan. What is not in the price is the decision itself and its size; if the market expected no cut, a 25-30% cut would look like the 2023/2024 prints (about -1%); if it already holds a cut, a modest trim or a hold reads as relief, which is what the +1.25% after the July miss looked like.
evidence.independence: Company precedent for cutting at Q3: https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/22110/140120231023569759.pdf (2023-10-24); for holding at Q3 and cutting in January: https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/22110/140120241012597517.pdf and https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/22110/140120250124555134.pdf. Quarterly OP series from https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=2211. Same company, separate documents.

evidence.text: The company's own 2026-07-28 差異 notice says beverage shipments have run above plan since June with summer supply in place at the new natural-water bottling plant, 洋菓子 store traffic has been recovering since June on lower-price products and new-format stores, confectionery has a new sales channel from Q3, and chocolate raw-material costs are easing, so Q3 OP is likely to improve on last year's -133m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 prints moved -1.06% (2023), -0.87% (2024), -0.77% (2025-10-28) on the Yahoo bars; no Q3 has been a positive surprise in the sample, so there is no measured reaction to a better Q3.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is the company's own guidance language and so sits inside what holders were told to expect, which is why it is sized small. What would be new is the Q3 number confirming it: a positive Q3 OP would be the first in the sample and would make the H2 plan look less hopeless; the flat tape (+0.44% over 20 days) says nobody has positioned for it either way.
evidence.independence: Cocoa futures have fallen through 2026 (https://cropgpt.ai/cocoa-near-two-year-lows-on-surplus-ghana-cuts-farmgate-as-ivory-coast-buys-back-stocks, undated snippet, macro proxy); no company or counterparty document after July corroborates the Q3 trend.

evidence.text: If the plan is held at Q3 as in 2024, the FY cut is likely to come in a separate 業績予想の修正 in late January (2024-01-26, 2025-01-27 precedents), each followed by about -1% to -2.5%.

FY IFIS consensus OP 56,150m / ordinary 62,350m (2026-10-23) vs company 55,000 / 58,000 https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=6923 . The H1 street bar has a single source and is three months old, so the findings that depend on it are capped small. My estimate is H1 OP about 18.0-18.5bn: roughly +6-9% vs the company plan and about -6% vs the street.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: JPX short register 2026-10-23: no disclosed position at or above 0.5% (short_ratio 0.0, change 0.0), source https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html via the sealed baseline. Margin ratio (信用倍率) 1.57, per kabutan 2026-10-26 https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=6923 : mildly long, not crowded. No options, so no skew. priced_lean -0.08. Run-up -0.33% over 20 days, -2.19% over 5. The sealed spot 3,572 already includes today's -1.3% morning drop (previous close 3,620), which was a down US tape (Dow -1.24%).

evidence.text: Q1 OP was 8,760m, 51.5% of the 17,000m H1 guide (prior years' Q1 share of actual H1 OP: 46.6% in FY26, about 50% in FY25), so H1 should beat the company plan. It is less clear H1 reaches the July IFIS bar of 19,500m, which needs a 10.7bn Q2 against 9.86bn last year: the late-July 2026 Kumamoto earthquake stopped Japanese auto lines in August (Honda Japan production -32.3%, Honda China -71.7%), partly offset by Honda North America (+19.0% Jul, +8.2% Aug) and a Q2 USD/JPY around 159 vs about 147 a year earlier.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026-07-30: OP beat IFIS by 6% and the guide was held, stock -3.78% (D-1 close to D+1 close). H1 2024-10-28: guide held, -0.50%. H1 2023-10-31: big beat on the H1 plan plus raises, +13.4%. Computed from the Yahoo daily bars https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/6923.T?range=3y&interval=1d
evidence.why_not_priced: Part of it is priced. The Honda and industry production data were published on 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-19, and the stock has slipped from 3,652 (10-19) to 3,572. Had the market fully marked H1 below the street, the IFIS FY ordinary consensus would have come down. It stayed at 62,350 for four weeks (kabuyoho, 10-23), so the street number has not absorbed the August stoppages.
evidence.independence: Honda's monthly data, reported by LOGISTICS TODAY https://www.logi-today.com/1005505 (2026-09-30) and https://www.logi-today.com/993639 (2026-08-31), and the industry quake attribution from MONOist https://monoist.itmedia.co.jp/mn/articles/2610/19/news020.html (2026-10-19). These are separate sources from the company document.

evidence.text: The FY27 plan assumes USD/JPY 150 with a sensitivity of about +3億 OP per yen per year. Q1 averaged 160.54, Jul-Sep averaged about 159, and spot is about 157, so FX alone gives the company room to raise FY OP by roughly 2-2.5bn (to about 57-57.5bn, above the 56.15bn street) at this print, if Japan and China do not consume it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2025-10-31: FY OP raised 41.2bn to 45.0bn plus a dividend raise, +2.33%. FY24 and FY25 plans were held all year with no reaction-moving revision. The company missed its own FY plan in FY25 (490 vs 500) and in FY26 (426 vs 450), per the kabuyoho revision history https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/report?bcode=6923 , so a hold, which is the base case, is not a surprise.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street FY OP (56.15bn) sits only 2% above the plan even though H1 FX ran 10 yen weaker than assumed. If a FX-driven raise were priced, consensus would be nearer 57-58bn. Against this, the company's record of missing its own plans is a reason the street holds back.
evidence.independence: USD/JPY monthly averages from Yahoo https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/JPY=X?range=6mo&interval=1d ; the Q1 FX table in https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260730/140120260730503602.pdf (the same company as the source, different document).

evidence.text: The FY27 capital-allocation page of the 2026-05-22 mid-term plan earmarks 300-350億 for dividends plus buybacks ('自己株式取得 継続的かつ機動的に実施'). The 111-yen dividend on about 126m shares is about 140億, which implies roughly 160-210億 (about 3.6-4.7% of the 4,500億 market cap) of buyback. None had been announced as of 2026-10-26 morning: the kabutan disclosure list from April to October shows only treasury-stock disposals for compensation.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-06-10: an 800億 buyback announced alongside a guide cut, +2.56% (D-1 to D+1). 2026-05-12: FY results with a dividend raise and the +29% OP guide, +12.87%. Earlier buybacks were announced at varied times (100億 in Feb 2023, per kabutan https://s.kabutan.jp/news/n202302040195/ ), so the H1 print is a possible date, not a fixed one.
evidence.why_not_priced: The plan is public, so the existence of a buyback is partly priced. Its timing is not. Probability-weighted at about 25-30% for today, it is worth roughly +3-4% if it lands and near 0 if it does not. The balance sheet (equity ratio 49.4% vs a 50% target after the 770億 Iwasaki deal, planned FCF -670億) argues against an early announcement, which is why the probability is low.
evidence.independence: The kabutan disclosure list https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=6923&nmode=3 (no 自己株式取得 notice since April 2026); the FY26 total-return history (283.9%) in https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260512/140120260512524373.pdf

options.reason: No liquid single-stock option market in Japan for this name. JPX option volume is concentrated in the index, so there is no event-implied move and no skew. Until 2026-09-18 that left priced_lean_pct as -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, which is ALSO the free control, so the baseline's lean and its own benchmark were the same number. They are no longer: `positioning` and `expected_move` below carry substitutes built from what Tokyo does publish, and this baseline supplies its own `priced_lean_pct` and `anchor_quality`.

history.caveat: Announcement DATES are estimated by applying this quarter's notified lag backwards to prior period ends; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate. This is a cadence prior, not a record that a print happened on that date. Use it as a scale for how much this name moves, never as evidence about a particular past date.

event_plausibility.basis: issuer-notified date carried by JPX on the 決算発表予定日 sheet

positioning.basis: absent from the JPX register, so no disclosed position at or above the 0.5% threshold. A real zero, not missing data -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0.
positioning.margin_ratio_basis: 信用倍率, margin long balance / margin short balance, scraped from a broker portal rather than published by the exchange. Null is a normal outcome.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of twelve ESTIMATED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it, and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read researcher_japan/scripts/jp_priced_in.py, lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR, none is measured on Japanese data, and jp_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them.
